unit.name: Why base LLMs need augmentation
unit.description: Motivation for augmenting pre-trained LLMs: limitations of control, domain coverage, freshness, task specificity, context handling, and the two optimization axes.
unit.summary: The lecture frames the session as a practical tour of techniques for building LLM applications beyond the base model, including prompting, RAG, agentic workflows, evals, and multi-agent systems [ts=5s]. Students identify base-model limitations such as missing domain knowledge, distribution shift, lack of current information, and poor fit for narrow enterprise tasks [ts=228s]. The instructor adds control failures, style/format inconsistency, task-specific understanding, limited context windows, and source requirements as recurring reasons a vanilla LLM underperforms [ts=475s]. RAG is previewed as a way to retrieve compressed document representations and attach relevant evidence to the prompt, but the lecture also notes latency and future-proofing debates [ts=856s]. The segment closes with a two-axis mental model: improve the foundation model itself, or improve how context and tools wrap around it through better prompts, RAG, agents, and multi-agent systems [ts=1001s].

key_points.text: The lecture goal is breadth over end-to-end product building: prompting techniques, agentic workflows, multi-agent systems, and evals.
Base models can lack domain knowledge or fail on domain-specific data not represented in public training sets.
Pre-trained models can be stale because retraining from scratch for every new trend is impractical.
LLMs are difficult to control, and even large teams struggle to prevent unwanted or biased outputs.
Limited context handling prevents standalone LLMs from reading thousands of enterprise documents directly.
RAG embeds documents, retrieves relevant representations, adds them as context, and supports sourcing.
LLM performance can improve either by using a stronger foundation model or by improving context, tools, prompts, RAG, and workflows around the model.

kp_catalog.name: LLM augmentation motivation
kp_catalog.description: Reasons a base LLM may need augmentation: control, domain gaps, freshness, style constraints, task-specific understanding, context limits, and sourcing needs.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: LLM augmentation motivates the lecture but is not itself a prerequisite gate.

kp_catalog.name: Context-window and attention limits
kp_catalog.description: The limitation that long contexts are finite and attention may miss relevant facts inside large corpora, motivating chunking, retrieval, and RAG-style systems.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor explicitly says enterprise knowledge management cannot be solved by a standalone LLM because context windows are limited [ts=681s].

kp_catalog.name: Model versus context optimization
kp_catalog.description: A two-axis mental model for improving LLM applications: better base models versus better prompts, tools, RAG, workflows, and multi-agent systems around the model.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: This model organizes the lecture's vertical axis of context/tool optimization after distinguishing it from foundation model improvements [ts=1001s].
